newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds moderately off in light trade.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds moderately off in light trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities tallied moderate losses in very thin trading Monday, traders and analysts said.
A few players shuffled paper ahead of Tuesday's consumer price data, leaving spreads over Treasuries steady to slightly wider.
"It's extremely quiet," one Ginnie trader said.
Tuesday's report on the March performance of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) should infuse some pep into pass-through trading, with risk seen mainly to the downside.

Economists in a Reuters poll forecast CPI rose 0.2 percent last month against a 0.3 percent increase the month before. They projected the core rate, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, climbed 0.3 percent versus 0.2 percent.
While that consensus seemed priced into the market, any unanticipated jump in the core rate could prompt selling on fears of further Federal Reserve tightenings, traders said.
"A strong CPI would hurt (prices)," another trader said.
A bearish price report could focus more attention on adjustable-rate products, adding to any losses in fixed-rate mortgages, he said.
Late Monday afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0-percent paper was off 1/32 at 100-15/32 to yield 112 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were off 2/32 at 100-16/32, and Freddie Mac 8.0s were down 1/32 at 100-23/32.
Five-year Treasuries were off 2/32 at 6.86 percent, and 10-year notes were down 2/32 at 6.98 percent.
